assertion_analysis.fails_if: A matching record is refused, no file is reported, or stored head/reviewer identity changes; the head equality itself echoes the supplied head and is only a persistence control.
Stale filing is accepted, produces no single refusal, or omits either independently planted earlier/current revision; removing the delivery guard and store guard restores these failures.
Refused stale filing overwrites the independently captured earlier record bytes or creates a current-head store record.

Either store accepts the earlier head, omits either revision in its exception, overwrites the earlier record or creates the committed-root directory on refusal; removing the matching store insertion restores acceptance.
Choosing the moving source brief rather than the dispatch snapshot raises on the matching snapshot record; the explicit stored-head equality only tests round-trip identity.
Replacing same_revision with strict equality refuses a full head matching an abbreviated brief; the stored-head equality itself echoes input.
The committed store refuses a matching record or persists a different head; equality alone does not test stale-head refusal.
Removing the run-directory fallback lets stale records be stored after pointer retirement.
Removing the explicit reviewer-context check lets an identity-omitting stale delivery file, loses the expected head in the refusal, or overwrites the earlier record.

findings.text: non-blocking: The stored-head equality assertions here and at lines 143, 149 and 156 compare with the same world["head"] supplied to the writer; these assertions alone survive removing the filing guard and should be counted as round-trip controls, with the mismatch/refusal assertions carrying the regression proof.
